stem: During a unit safety discussion, nurses identify a recurring client-care process problem that has contributed to several near misses. Which action best reflects the RN's role in performance improvement?

options.A: Report the identified care-process problem to the appropriate personnel and participate in efforts to improve the process
options.B: Avoid reporting the pattern unless a client is actually harmed
options.C: Treat each near miss as unrelated and make no attempt to address the recurring process problem
options.D: Wait for non-nursing personnel to identify and correct the problem because performance improvement is outside the RN role

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places Performance Improvement within Management of Care and expects the RN to identify and report client-care issues or problems and participate in performance-improvement and quality-improvement processes. Therefore A is the best answer. Waiting for actual harm, ignoring a recurring pattern, or treating performance improvement as outside nursing practice conflicts with the RN role described by NCSBN.
educational_objective: Participate in performance improvement by reporting recurring client-care process problems and contributing to corrective quality-improvement efforts before harm occurs.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

source_claim_supported: The RN has a role in identifying and reporting client-care process problems and participating in performance-improvement/quality-improvement activities.

correction_summary: Removed the weak recall question about the institutional purpose of a daily safety huddle and the broad TeamSTEPPS locator. Rebuilt the item around the RN's explicit 2026 NCSBN role when a recurring safety problem is identified during team communication.
audit_findings: A directly matches the NCSBN Performance Improvement activity statements. B incorrectly requires actual harm before reporting; C ignores a recurring systems pattern; D falsely excludes the RN from performance improvement. The scenario does not depend on a specific meeting format, facility policy, or branded teamwork model. No second-answer ambiguity or unresolved source conflict remains.
